summary: Klaus Butzenberger is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who completed his Magisterprüfung at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm. He held teaching posts at Munich, Free University of Berlin, and Humboldt University, and held a chair at Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Fischer worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University and studying under Jitendra Nath Banerjea and Ordhendra Coomar Gangoly. He held a post at the German Archaeological Institute and was a professor at Bonn (1966–1985).

Klaus Hahlweg specialized in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Munich in 1954 under Helmut Hoffmann.

Klaus Karttunen works in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned his BA at the University of Helsinki, studying under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola, and held research and professorial posts at Helsinki and the Academy of Finland.

Indologist Klaus Ludwig Janert studied at Halle, Frankfurt, Tübingen, and Göttingen, where he completed his PhD under Paul Thieme. He served as an assistant and library staff at Göttingen, PD at Tübingen, and ordinary professor of Indology at Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Matzel worked in linguistics and Indology, completing his Ph.D. at Free University of Berlin and habilitation at Würzburg. He taught at Berlin and Peradeniya before serving as Professor of Germanic Philology at the University of Regensburg (1968–1989).

Klaus Mylius worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Karl Ammer and Friedrich Weller at Halle and Leipzig. He served as Hochschuldozent at Leipzig (1970–1991) and Lehrbeauftragter at Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and held a postdoctoral teaching post there in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Bertold Spuler, Wolfgang Lentz, and Annemarie von Gabain, completed his habilitation at Giessen, and was professor of Turkology at Göttingen (1992–2003).

Indologist Klaus Rüping studied at Bonn and Münster, where he completed his PhD in 1968 and studied under Paul Hacker in 1963. He spent his career at the University of Münster, becoming ordinary professor in 1980.
Klaus Strunk was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Karl Hoffmann around 1957–1961. He held academic posts at Saarland University (1968–1977) and the University of Munich (1977–1998).

Klaus Wille is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He worked on manuscript cataloguing with the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1997 and held research posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2026).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Klaus Sagaster and Michael Hahn, earning degrees at Bonn, Marburg, and Hamburg, and held professorships at the University of Vienna and the University of Hong Kong.

Klaus-Josef Notz worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a Diplom in theology at PTH Benediktbeuern and a Doctor theologiae at the University of Munich, where he served as Lehrbeauftragter in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Uppsala University by 2000, under the doctoral supervision of Peter Schalk.

Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD at UC Santa Barbara. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (from 1996) and the University of Oslo (1996–1999).

Knut Kristiansen worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Georg Morgenstierne at the University of Oslo, where he subsequently served as Universitetslektor in modern Indian languages from 1971 to 1998.

Kobun Otogawa was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kodo Sawaki and Gadjin Nagao, earning degrees from Komazawa and Kyoto Universities. He taught at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center, Haiku Zendo, and Naropa University.

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership posts at Komazawa University, including president in 1909, and lectured at Tokyo University.
Kodo Kawamura was a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his master's and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1968 to 2004.
